Workbook Quality Checks D34 defines the single-bar test; Internal Quality Checks E34 permits shared flows, with qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md preserving separately scored outcomes. The actual successful controls remain mandatory at prompt.md:25,100. Concrete branch checks: judge.toml:49,56 and prompt.md:148-149 distinguish stopped-handler suppression from retaining the successful picture; disabled/static content may satisfy suppression but cannot excuse an empty/hidden retained preview. judge.toml:91,98 and prompt.md:205-210 give one conditional preview rule: explicit execution refusal restores last-good, whereas caught blocked networking may complete valid authored code; both attempts still require actual blocked/refused evidence. judge.toml:119,126,133 and prompt.md:225-236 keep all five unsupported-family refusals mandatory, while the ordinary-code fallback supplies a control when the separately scored harmless-word feature fails. History checks retain one bar: judge.toml:504-581 and prompt.md:464-480 require actual accepted snapshots, original-result retries, unchanged newer heads, stale refusal, real-editor draft preservation, and one accepted race winner for their respective owners. In particular judge.toml:532 and prompt.md:470-471 require both captured-request cases and the real lost-reply user path; automatic recovery is an explicit supported way to satisfy the same retry outcome. Polish judge.toml:23,41,50,59 allows tabs/drawers/scrolling, composite keyboard navigation, native focus, and standard editor escape while retaining each named outcome. Visual judge.toml:24-29,39-44,54-59,69-74,84-89,99-104 supplies one anchor-5 definition per criterion; simple/native styling and harmless imperfections are compatible examples, not a second weaker target. Adversarial source thought experiments (not executed app runs): an app that immediately refuses every loop cannot earn deadline credit because judge.toml:140 and prompt.md:242-267 require three successful computed finite-loop controls; a restore implementation that replays requests correctly but offers neither automatic recovery nor a usable lost-reply retry fails judge.toml:532/prompt.md:471. Conversely a conforming automatic retry with no manual button, or a static last-good snapshot with disabled handlers, is explicitly permitted and cannot be failed merely for those implementation choices.
